sections.html:
The City of Detroit bills its own property tax through the Office of the Treasury, and the Wayne County Treasurer takes over once a bill goes delinquent. The Office of the Assessor sets the values. Use the due dates printed on your Detroit bill, and ask the Office of the Treasury if a date is unclear.

Wayne County's treasurer states the handoff rule plainly: any bill still open with the city after the end of February turns delinquent on March 1, and from that day only the county accepts payment. Detroit joined the county's Delinquent Tax Revolving Fund program with tax year 2003, under Public Act 246.

sections.h2: What happens when Detroit property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
A Detroit parcel can go from delinquent to foreclosed in about two years, and the interest climbs at each step. Wayne County's treasurer describes the sequence this way.

Delinquent tax stages for Detroit parcels, per the Wayne County Treasurer
StageTimingWhat changes
DelinquentMarch 1 after the tax yearPayable only to Wayne County; interest at 1% a month
ForfeitedThe next March 1Interest becomes 1.5% a month, back to the original delinquency date, plus a $175 foreclosure fee and $30 in recording fees
ForeclosedMarch 31 after a year in forfeiture, in an uncontested caseTitle goes to the Wayne County Treasurer and a judgment is recorded
AuctionSeptember and October of that yearMinimum bid equals taxes, penalties, interest and costs

The office sends at least ten written notices before foreclosure, four during the first year of delinquency and six after forfeiture. A foreclosed parcel is first offered to the state, the city, the county or an authority at the minimum bid, and anything left goes to the September and October auctions, where winning bidders receive a quit claim deed. The county also says it cannot waive penalties and interest on a current bill.

sections.h2: What help exists for Detroit owners behind on tax?
sections.html:
Wayne County runs payment plans for owners who occupy their homes and face financial hardship. The county's income standard is 125% of the federal poverty level, and applicants with income just above that line are told to apply anyway. Staff review the file and reply within 30 days of receiving it.

  • Applicants need a Michigan driver's license or state ID, a copy of the deed, proof that the home is the principal residence, and proof of income.
  • Owners by recorded deed or land contract can qualify.
  • The Poverty Tax Exemption comes from the local assessing unit, so Detroit residents ask the city's assessor, not the county.
  • Calls to the treasurer's taxpayer assistance line go to (313) 224-5990, and email goes to taxinfo@waynecountymi.gov.
  • The same office can send text reminders about plan payments, which you can request by phone or email.
  • A hardship extension that was granted and paid off in an earlier year does not bar a new application if hardship continues.

When the owner has died and the house is still in a relative's name, the treasurer points families to Lakeshore Legal Aid at 888-783-8190 and the Wayne County Probate Court at 313-224-5706. For title help, the county's FAQ lists United Community Housing Coalition at (313) 963-3310 and Legal Aid and Defender at (313) 964-4130.

sections.h2: Where does a Detroit assessment appeal begin?
sections.html:
Detroit assessment appeals start with the city's Board of Review and can continue to the Michigan Tax Tribunal, the two bodies that Wayne County's treasurer names as able to change a tax figure. The county treasurer cannot reduce a bill once it is issued.

Ask the Office of the Assessor for the current filing window and forms, because the dates change by year.

sections.h2: How do Detroit size and layout affect a seller?
sections.html:
Detroit covers 142.87 square miles, of which 138.75 are land, along the Detroit River in the southeast corner of Michigan. The ground slopes gently from the northwest toward the river on a clay till plain, and the French established Fort Pontchartrain du Detroit on July 24, 1701. The climate is hot-summer humid continental, with temperatures staying below freezing on about 44 days a year.

Neighborhoods vary a great deal. Downtown, Midtown, Corktown and New Center are dense and historic, Lafayette Park is a Mies van der Rohe district, and southwest Detroit has seen new housing and business openings. Meanwhile, parts of the northeast and the city's fringes have large numbers of vacant lots. Because the city is so large, a single price is a poor guide: compare your own block.

The employment base is automotive, finance, technology and health care. Midtown's Detroit Medical Center is the largest single employer, and General Motors, Rocket Mortgage, Ally Financial and DTE Energy are among the companies headquartered in the city. The Detroit Department of Transportation runs buses within city limits, SMART connects the suburbs, and the QLINE streetcar runs along the central corridor. Four border crossings link the city to Windsor, and the Gordie Howe International Bridge is listed as opened in 2026.

sections.h2: How do Detroit housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a city whose figures sit far from its suburbs'. The July 2025 estimate for Detroit is 649,095 people, a gain of 1.5% since the 2020 census base.

  • Owner-held houses carry a median value of $83,900 for 2020-2024, against $354,500 in Farmington Hills.
  • Owners occupy 50.3% of housing, across 257,998 households.
  • Households have a median income of $39,938, and 32.7% of people fall below the poverty line.
  • Renters pay a median of $1,074 a month.

Where values run this low, an overdue balance of a few thousand dollars can take a big bite out of a sale price. Request the exact payoff early.

sections.h2: How is the tax balance cleared at a Detroit closing?
sections.html:
Under MCL 211.135 a register of deeds asks for treasurer certificates covering tax liens and a five-year tax history before a deed is recorded. A warranty deed can be refused until they are in the file. Quitclaim deeds and some other conveyances are excepted.

Deed certification happens at Wayne County's Treasurer's Office, 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit, MI 48226, for $5 a document with up to 25 parcel numbers and 20 cents for each parcel beyond that. Only originals qualify, never copies. The certified deed then moves on to the county's recording office, which needs its own appointment.

Delinquent payments by bank transfer online cost nothing, while cards add 2.49%, which goes to the service provider. Wayne County warns that its staff never come to a home to collect money, so pay only at the office, online, at an authorized kiosk or by mail.

faqs.q: Who takes payment on delinquent Detroit property tax?
faqs.a: The Wayne County Treasurer. Unpaid bills turn delinquent on March 1 and are payable only to the county from then on. The office is at 400 Monroe Street, 5th Floor, Detroit, and takes calls at (313) 224-5990.

faqs.q: How fast can Detroit tax foreclosure happen?
faqs.a: Roughly two years. A parcel forfeits on the March 1 after delinquency begins, then can be foreclosed the following March 31 in an uncontested case, with auctions in September and October.

faqs.q: What interest applies to delinquent Detroit property tax?
faqs.a: Interest runs 1% a month at first, then 1.5% a month once the parcel is forfeited, applied back to the date the tax became delinquent. A $175 fee and $30 recording fee are added at forfeiture.

faqs.q: Can a Detroit house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Proceeds cover the balance at the closing table, and the title company relies on the treasurer's certification. Ask Wayne County for a written payoff first, because interest keeps adding up.

faqs.q: Does Detroit offer relief from property tax?
faqs.a: Possibly. Wayne County runs payment plans for owner-occupants, and the Poverty Tax Exemption is requested through the city's assessing office. Ask the Office of the Assessor for the current application.
